title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. 𝔾 is a profinite group, normal in a larger group G_{ρ,σ}. 𝔾 is probably the profinite completion of SL(2,ℤ)', i.e. a free profinite group of rank 2; the margin note covers the case 𝔾 = SL(2,Ẑ)'. ρ and σ are distinguished elements acting on 𝔾 by conjugation, presumably the order-4 and order-6 elements of SL(2,ℤ). For a suitable u, u_{ξ,η} denotes the automorphism (an element of G_{ρ,σ}) determined by u(ρ)=ξρ, u(σ)=ησ. B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} is the group of such u whose pair (u(ρ)ρ^{-1}, u(σ)σ^{-1}) lies in a prescribed set Σ_{ρ,σ} of 'admissible' pairs; these are solutions of the loop equation ('équation des lacets'), with the ε_1^ν / L_1 condition of p. 507. 𝒢_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ}×G_{ρ,σ} is the set of conjugator pairs (α,β) with αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1}ε_1^ν.

On this page:

(31) The commutator map 𝒢_{ρ,σ} → Σ_{ρ,σ}, (α,β) ↦ (ξ,η). Here ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} = [α,ρ] = α(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = [β,σ] = β(σ)σ^{-1}.

(32) The hypothesis (each admissible pair is realised by a unique automorphism) gives a canonical diagonal section (ξ,η) ↦ (u_{ξ,η}, u_{ξ,η}).

Theorem. Put Z_ρ = Centr_{G_{ρ,σ}}(ρ) and Z_σ = Centr_{G_{ρ,σ}}(σ). In the SL(2,Ẑ)' case Z_ρ = T_ρ and Z_σ = N'_σ. Then (34), B_{ρ,σ}×Z_ρ×Z_σ → 𝒢_{ρ,σ}, (u,a,b) ↦ (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}), is a bijection. The reason is that the fibre of the commutator map α ↦ αρα^{-1} over uρu^{-1} is the coset u·Z_ρ, and likewise for σ. So the solution set is a 'torsor-like' product of the group B of admissible automorphisms with the two centralizers.

Corollary (begun). Let δ_G : G_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/𝔾 be the quotient map, and let δ_B, δ_ρ, δ_σ be its restrictions to B, Z_ρ, Z_σ. A margin note says Z_ρ → B and Z_σ → B are injective (35).

The next page forms the fibre product B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ (a group). Via (34) and (38) it transports a group structure onto the set of conjugator pairs. The resulting composition law is (α',β')(α,β) = (u'(α)α', u'(β)β'). This has exactly the shape of the Drinfeld/Ihara composition law of GT, (λ1,f1)(λ2,f2) = (λ1λ2, f1·σ1(f2)), written here as a semidirect product of automorphisms and conjugators. Exact sequences follow, with kernel L_0 and centralizer pieces.

Purpose: to give the set of solutions of the loop equation, with their choices of conjugators, a natural group structure, as an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ}. This is a GT-type group seen through SL(2,Ẑ) and its torsion elements.
errors: Notational inconsistency: the theorem defines Z_ρ, Z_σ, but the product in (34) is written B_{ρ,σ}×T_ρ×T_σ. This only matches the margin's special case Z_ρ = T_ρ, Z_σ = N'_σ (note: T_σ, not N'_σ).

Bijectivity of (34) silently requires that u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ]) identify B_{ρ,σ} with Σ_{ρ,σ}. This means uniqueness of u_{ξ,η}, i.e. the automorphism being determined by the images of ρ and σ, which is the role of the 'hypothesis'. Existence alone would give only surjectivity.
'G_{ρ,σ} = G' in the corollary must mean the quotient G_{ρ,σ}/𝔾 = Γ_{ρ,σ}, given that δ_G is called the canonical quotient homomorphism.

Small gap: the claim that the pairs (ξ,η) from (α,β) ∈ 𝒢 lie in Σ is justified only 'par définition de B'. It actually uses the defining relation of 𝒢 (the ε_1^ν condition) together with 𝔾 being normal.

ideas.what: Fibre of the commutator/conjugation map is a coset of the centralizer, giving 𝒢_{ρ,σ} ≅ B×Z_ρ×Z_σ
Group structure on pairs (automorphism, conjugators) as a fibre product B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ, with composition (α',β')(α,β) = (u'(α)α', u'(β)β')
ideas.modern_name: group law of GT-type groups (Drinfeld's (λ,f) composition, 'pairs with conjugators')
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme (1984); no explicit formula published to my knowledge

ideas.what: Working with SL(2,Ẑ)' (free profinite of rank 2) and the torsion elements ρ (order 4) and σ (order 6), with centralizers T_ρ and N'_σ
ideas.modern_name: GT action on the profinite completion of SL2(ℤ) / Γ_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and Γ_{1,1}, but not this computation

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a GT-like group as a fibre product of an automorphism group with the centralizers of two torsion elements of SL(2,Ẑ), mapping to a common quotient Γ_{ρ,σ}. This is a modular-group-centred presentation of 'loop equation' solutions. It parallels, but is formulated differently from, the later Lochak–Schneps/Nakamura treatments. The content is largely routine group theory, but the specific packaging (SΓ, exact sequences with L_0 and SZ_ρ×SZ_σ) is not in the literature as such.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's independent route to GT-type groups via SL(2,Ẑ) and the centralizers of its elements of order 4 and 6. This is of historical interest for the pre-Drinfeld genesis of GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The theorem on this page is a straightforward orbit–stabilizer decomposition. The only notable content is historical: an early, independent formalism for the group law on loop-equation solutions with conjugators, centred on SL(2,Ẑ). That is broadly consistent with what is already known of Grothendieck's GT ideas.
transcription_corrections: In (31) the image reads ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} = [α,ρ] = α(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = βσ(β)^{-1} = [β,σ] = β(σ)σ^{-1}, not 'αρα^{-1}' / 'βσβ^{-1}'.
The source of (31) and target of (32) is the script set 𝒢_{ρ,σ} (pairs), not the group G_{ρ,σ}.
In the theorem the margin reads 'Z_ρ = T_ρ, Z_σ = N'_σ' within 'NB dans le cas 𝔾 = SL(2,Ẑ)' etc, on a…'.
The corollary line should read 'δ_G l'hom. canonique de passage au quotient G_{ρ,σ} → G_{ρ,σ}/𝔾 = Γ_{ρ,σ}' (the transcription's 'G_{ρ,σ} = G' garbles this).
The page heading looks like '55f' or '557'; this is uncertain.
